# A guide on how to plan a group trip that will actually happen.

6 min read

Image: Blane Bachelor Author avatar

Blane Bachelor
July 21, 2026

Some of my best travel experiences have been with others. Girlfriend getaways in California. A Jamaican road trip with three adventurous buddies. London with extended family.

But a great group trip takes effort to make happen. Here’s how to plan it well – whoever you’re traveling with and wherever you go.

## Tips for planning a great group trip.

### Establish the key components early.

Once you have a core group interested (about 3 or 4 people), you can start hashing out the most important elements of your trip:

  * Budget: Determine a price range everyone is willing to spend
  * Vibe: Is your crew craving a tropical beach getaway? A European city break with world-class museums and restaurants? A carefree road trip?
To avoid this common dilemma, put these tips into your group trip toolbox:

  * Make sure deposits are paid early. This way, you’ll avoid last-minute changes – especially if they’re non-refundable.
  * Ask a couple of enthusiastic people to be vocal about their RSVPs early. This is what the group chat is made for. Seeing everyone else make plans and get excited can be the nudge the undecided need.

### Plan your trip early (but embrace impromptu getaways, too.)

In my experience, most group trips need at least four to six months’ advance planning – maybe even more if you’re headed abroad.

This has several advantages. First, it gives you plenty of time to take care of the logistics – like booking flights, hotels and creating an itinerary. Second, it allows for wiggle room for changes or more people who decide to join. And finally, you’ll have enough time to secure sought-after reservations – as well as better deals on flights and hotels.

That said, last-minute getaways can work if dates align. --------------------------------------------------------------------------------
